claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model without a material-weakness disclosure is compliant and evidentially supported despite an unresolved Spanish-language billing support gap tied to named international pilot commitments.
specific_concerns: The available record supports aggregate readiness, but not a clean conclusion that no disclosure issue exists.
The affected segment is named in three international pilot commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for named launch use cases.
Legal review is still open, and the policy says pending legal review does not resolve materiality.
No approved risk acceptance is identified in the admissible record.
Public guidance on monitored deployment and documentation is general and does not override the internal policy predicate for disclosure.

unsupported_claims: Any claim that the Spanish-language billing support gap is immaterial based solely on low projected traffic share or non-core labeling.
Any claim that certification without material-weakness disclosure is fully supported by the admissible record.
Any claim that public AI guidance alone satisfies the internal policy requirement for disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: The actual legal review outcome on whether the Spanish-language billing gap requires disclosure.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering the named launch use case before launch.
The underlying contractual or pilot commitment documents showing how Spanish-language billing support is described.
The full policy text and any implementing guidance defining disclosure thresholds for named launch use cases.
The underlying evaluation data for the 2.1-point miss and any remediation timeline tied to launch.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the action satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Certification without disclosure would need evidence of either resolution of the limitation or approved risk acceptance before launch.
General external guidance can support process quality, but cannot substitute for the required internal support link.
